learn.title: Electric Buses and Trucks Explained
learn.intro: Electrifying commercial vehicles cuts emissions and reduces fossil fuel dependence. With rising urbanization, shifting to electric buses and trucks is vital for sustainable cities and cleaner freight transport.
learn.c1_text: Electric buses and trucks produce no tailpipe emissions, unlike diesel vehicles. For example, a single electric bus can save 1.5 tons of CO2 annually compared to a diesel counterpart.
learn.c2_text: Electric vehicles (EVs) have fewer moving parts, reducing maintenance costs by up to 40%. Charging is also cheaper than refueling diesel, making long-term savings significant.
learn.c3_text: India aims to electrify 50% of its public transport by 2025. Cities like Delhi have deployed over 5,000 electric buses, supported by subsidies under the FAME II scheme.
learn.stat1: India plans to add 10,000 electric buses by 2025.
learn.stat2: Electric trucks can reduce fuel costs by 50% over their lifecycle.
learn.stat3: Global electric truck sales grew 60% in 2023.
learn.stat4: Charging an electric bus costs ~₹3 per km vs. ₹15 for diesel.

learn.title: Rooftop Solar & Net Metering in India
learn.intro: Rooftop solar allows homes and businesses to generate clean energy, while net metering policies enable surplus power to be fed back to the grid, reducing bills and promoting decentralized energy.
learn.c1_text: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity via photovoltaic cells. A 5 kW system can power a typical home, generating ~7,000 kWh annually in sunny regions like Gujarat.
learn.c2_text: Net metering credits excess electricity sent to the grid. For example, if your system produces 100 kWh but you use 60 kWh, you’re credited for 40 kWh, offsetting future bills.
learn.c3_text: India’s net metering policy allows up to 100% of surplus power to be credited. Over 1.5 GW of rooftop solar is installed under this scheme, with states like Maharashtra leading adoption.
learn.stat1: India has 10 GW of rooftop solar installed (2024).
learn.stat2: Net metering reduces electricity bills by 30–50% for users.
learn.stat3: Rooftop solar accounts for 15% of India’s total solar capacity.
learn.stat4: Over 1 million households use rooftop solar in India.

learn.title: Small Wind Turbines for Homes
learn.intro: Small wind turbines generate electricity for homes or communities, reducing grid reliance. They are ideal for rural areas with consistent wind, offering a decentralized renewable energy solution.
learn.c1_text: Small turbines (5–100 kW) use wind to spin blades, generating electricity. A 10 kW turbine can power 2–3 homes, producing ~10,000 kWh annually in windy areas.
learn.c2_text: Community wind projects reduce energy costs and create local jobs. For example, a 50 kW turbine can power a small village, cutting reliance on diesel generators.
learn.c3_text: India has 400+ wind farms, but small turbines are underutilized. Policies like the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) aim to boost decentralized wind energy adoption.
learn.stat1: India’s wind energy capacity is 44 GW (2024).
learn.stat2: Small turbines can reduce electricity costs by 20–30%.
learn.stat3: Rural India spends ₹2,000 crore annually on diesel generators.
learn.stat4: Wind energy meets 30% of India’s renewable targets.
learn.readLabel: Read at US Dept of Energy

learn.title: Tidal Stream Energy Explained
learn.intro: Tidal stream energy harnesses ocean currents to generate predictable, clean power. It’s a promising solution for coastal regions, offering 24/7 energy with minimal environmental impact.
learn.c1_text: Tidal stream turbines are placed in ocean currents. A single turbine can generate 1–2 MW, enough to power 1,000 homes, with energy output predictable due to tidal cycles.
learn.c2_text: Tidal energy has low environmental impact. Turbines are designed to avoid marine life, and their placement is carefully planned to minimize disruption to ecosystems.
learn.c3_text: The UK’s MeyGen project generates 10 MW from tidal streams. India’s Andaman Islands are exploring tidal energy, with pilot projects underway to assess feasibility.
learn.stat1: Global tidal energy potential is 3,000 GW.
learn.stat2: Tidal turbines can operate 24/7, unlike solar or wind.
learn.stat3: India’s coastal zones have high tidal energy potential.
learn.stat4: Tidal energy costs are expected to drop 20% by 2030.

learn.title: Microgrids for Energy Independence
learn.intro: Microgrids provide localized energy independence, especially for villages and disaster-prone areas. They integrate renewables, storage, and smart controls to ensure resilience during grid outages.
learn.c1_text: A microgrid is a localized grid that can operate independently. It uses solar, wind, or diesel generators and stores energy in batteries for backup during outages.
learn.c2_text: After Hurricane Sandy, microgrids kept hospitals and schools running. In India, microgrids in rural areas ensure power during monsoon-related outages.
learn.c3_text: India has 1,000+ microgrids, with 50% in rural areas. The government’s PM-KUSUM scheme supports solar microgrids for farmers, reducing diesel use by 70%.
learn.stat2: Microgrids reduce energy costs by 40% in rural areas.
learn.stat3: Over 50% of microgrids in India use solar power.
learn.stat4: Microgrids can restore power within 10 minutes of an outage.
learn.readLabel: Read at US Dept of Energy

learn.title: Hydrogen Fuel Cells for Vehicles
learn.intro: Hydrogen fuel cells generate electricity by combining hydrogen and oxygen, producing only water as a byproduct. They offer a clean alternative for heavy-duty transport and long-haul vehicles.
learn.c1_text: Hydrogen fuel cells use a chemical reaction to produce electricity. A single cell generates 0.7 V, and stacks of cells power vehicles, with water as the only emission.
learn.c2_text: Fuel cell vehicles (FCVs) emit only water vapor. A Toyota Mirai, for example, produces 0.05 kg of CO2 per km, compared to 0.18 kg for a diesel car.
learn.c3_text: India’s National Hydrogen Mission aims to produce 5 million tons of green hydrogen by 2030. Pilot projects in Gujarat and Tamil Nadu are testing FCVs for buses and trucks.
learn.stat1: India’s hydrogen energy potential is 400 GW.
learn.stat2: FCVs can travel 600 km on a single tank of hydrogen.
learn.stat3: Global hydrogen fuel cell vehicle sales reached 10,000 in 2023.
learn.stat4: Hydrogen production costs are expected to drop 30% by 2030.
